newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FORECAST-HK property sector net to grow 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-HK property sector net to grow 17 pct.

text.p: Hong Kong property companies should see annual net profit growth of 17 percent for the industry as a whole between 1996 and 1999, Lehman Brothers said on Wednesday.
Barring any unexpected shocks, the outlook for Hong Kong property companies is attractive, research analyst Patrick Chau told reporters.
"Our conclusion for the sector financials is very positive," said Chau.
After stripping out exceptionals, Lehman expects the underlying growth rate for earnings to be even stronger at 20 percent per year, he said.
He gave no comparative figures for previous years.

According to a Lehman Brothers study released on Wednesday, the growth forecasts are driven by an expected 20 percent increase in residential sales prices for the next two years and a rise in the volume of property for sale.

Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd is expected to be a top performer in the sector, and its shares should trade at HK$110 within 12 months, Lehman Brothers senior investment analyst Michael Leary told reporters.
